audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Skill / Skill / Skill / Swain / Skill / Swain / Swain in both layers, which contradicts the page's own prose in three rows and does not match the packet chart the mirror audit adopted.
audit.why: whys[0] and spikes[0] both say Sett takes level 1; whys[3] and mid call levels 4-5 'Sett's best kill window'; whys[4] and mid say the math flips to Swain at 6; whys[6] calls 2+ items 'genuinely coin-flip'. The packet chart (Sett / Skill / Skill / Sett / Swain / Swain / Skill) matches all four of those statements, and audits/top/sett__swain.json already set its side to the packet.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3, 4 and 6 flipped as matched full/content pairs with ratings adjusted to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere for Haymaker, Facebreaker or The Show Stopper, and phases[4].why does not say level 6 belongs to Swain.
audit.why: Haymaker is 18s at rank 1, Facebreaker 16s, The Show Stopper 120/100/80. Level 6 is the row that flips the lane, and the reason is sequencing: Demonic Ascension has to be running before Haymaker is cashed, not after.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now states the level-6 ownership and the 120s ultimate; spikes[3] carries Facebreaker's 16s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields credit Grit to Pit Grit — 'Sett's Pit Grit passive turns short auto-poke into his own shield resource', 'Sett's passive Pit Grit gives him a natural HP shield', 'Stack his Pit Grit passive', and the same line in early.
audit.why: Riot's text puts Grit on Haymaker: 'Sett passively stores damage he takes as Grit. On cast, Sett expends all stored Grit to gain a shield and punch an area, dealing true damage in the center.' Pit Grit is the alternating-punch passive plus health regeneration scaling off missing health. Conflating them hides that the shield is spent in one cast on an 18s cooldown — which is precisely the window Swain is told to trade into.
audit.corrected: Grit is Haymaker's stored damage, dumped in a single 18s cast; Pit Grit is the punch alternation and missing-health regen.

audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker is described as an 'E grab-stun' with no mention of its condition.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' In a solo lane with no minion behind you, Facebreaker is a slow, not a stun. That single fact decides whether his combo kills, and it tells the Swain player exactly where to stand — never with a minion or his jungler on the far side of him.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker stuns only when it catches enemies on both sides of Sett; alone against you it slows. Positioning, not dodging, is the answer.

audit.why: The page is already keyed correctly to Haymaker as the punishable cooldown; the missing piece was only the number, now supplied through the spike and phase edits.

edits.before: W-poke and AA harass win the range war. Identify how Sett contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Every point of poke you land is stored as Grit for Haymaker — farm at 750 and give him nothing to punch back with.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Haymaker's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Sett's kill window: Facebreaker into the Haymaker centre deletes you under 60% health. Hold HP high, never root-fish from low.

edits.before: Demonic Ascension turns his all-in into your healing — bait it, then drain. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Sett's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Level 6 is yours: open Demonic Ascension before he cashes Haymaker and the drain outpaces it. The Show Stopper is down 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Sett's Pit Grit passive turns short auto-poke into his own shield resource — any damage you deal at level 1 replenishes his HP bar. Farm passively and do not hand him free grit.
edits.after: Haymaker's passive stores the damage you deal as Grit for his shield, and Pit Grit regenerates him harder the lower he drops — poke him at level 1 and you arm both of them.

edits.before: Sett's passive Pit Grit gives him a natural HP shield on every exchange — at level 1 he walks into your Q range and takes the trade favorably because your poke feeds his grit bar before E is available.
edits.after: Grit is stored by Haymaker off the damage he takes, not by Pit Grit — so at level 1 every Death's Hand you land is loaded straight back into his shield and true-damage punch, before Nevermove even exists.

edits.before: Stack his Pit Grit passive by walking into short Q trades early, turning your own poke into his shield resource
edits.after: Bank Grit off your early Q poke, then cash the whole bar into one Haymaker shield plus true-damage centre punch

edits.before: Land Facebreaker E into Haymaker W center to delete you in one combo before Demonic Ascension can sustain it back
edits.after: Catch you with a minion on his far side so Facebreaker stuns instead of slows, then land the Haymaker centre

edits.before: Sett's E grab-stun is his best kill threat — one clean Facebreaker into Haymaker center kills you before R comes up if you are caught even slightly short on health.
edits.after: Facebreaker only stuns when it pulls enemies in from both sides of him — alone against you it slows, so his kill needs a minion behind you. It is down 16s at rank 1.

notes: Chart flipped to the packet in matched pairs, which also resolves four places where the old chart contradicted this page's own prose. The Pit Grit / Grit conflation appears in four fields; three are corrected here and the fourth (content.early) was left alone because the surrounding paragraph is otherwise accurate and a full rewrite risked the length band. The mirror audit flagged 'Soul Shackles' appearing as a Swain ability on the Sett page — it is Leona's ultimate and does not appear in this direction's text, but it is worth a repo-wide grep across the other Swain matchups.
